chunks: Ma'ani al-Akhbar: My father, from Sa'd, from Ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

In the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And the poets – only the astray follow them.' He said: Have you seen anyone following a poet? Rather, they are a group who gained understanding (became learned) for the sake of something other than the religion, so they themselves went astray and caused others to go astray.

key_terms.الْغَاوُونَ: the astray / those who go astray
key_terms.لِغَيْرِ الدِّينِ: for the sake of other than the religion / for worldly ends

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'astray' that follow poets according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) explains the Quranic verse regarding poets, noting that the 'astray' who follow them are not just any followers, but specifically those who acquired knowledge or eloquence for worldly or non-religious purposes, leading to their own misguidance and that of others.
